lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: narrowing or broadening an inquiry

studentTask.text: Today's focus: narrowing or broadening an inquiry. Essential question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to narrowing or broadening an inquiry change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim? By the end of this lesson you should be able to: Explain what narrowing or broadening an inquiry means and name the textual signal that tells you it is in play. You'll need: course notebook or digital equivalent; the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation; citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course.

guidedSupport.text:
Work through this with a facilitator, tutor, or on your own if you're ready:
- Welcome and retrieval: Open with a short retrieval prompt on today's lesson. Ask the learner to predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.
- Framing: State that today's material is deliberately outside the unit's practised range.
- Transfer task: Apply the move to an unfamiliar passage of comparable complexity with the checklist available. The task concerns today's lesson but the context is new. No worked example for this context is supplied to any course.
- Account of the transfer: The learner explains what carried over from the unit and what had to be adapted, and why.

If you get stuck:
- If prerequisite gap: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for today's lesson, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
- If repeated error pattern: Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of today's lesson.
- If procedure without understanding: Ask the learner to explain why the move for today's lesson works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
